speaker: Swami Sivananda
title: Discipline of speech
text: Speak the truth at all cost. Speak a little. Speak sweetly. Always utter encouraging words. Never condemn, criticize or discourage. Do not raise your voice and shout at little children or subordinates.
modern_interpretation: Communicate with unwavering honesty, even when it's challenging. Be concise and thoughtful in your words, ensuring they are always delivered with kindness and gentleness. Make it a practice to uplift and inspire others. Actively avoid judgment, criticism, or demoralizing remarks. Maintain a calm, respectful tone, especially when interacting with children or those in less powerful positions, demonstrating self-control and empathy.
summary: Practice disciplined speech by always being truthful, concise, kind, and encouraging. Avoid condemning, criticizing, or discouraging others, and maintain a respectful tone, especially with children and subordinates.
actionable_advice: Before speaking, pause and ask yourself if your words are truthful, kind, necessary, and helpful, especially when addressing someone with less power.
embedding_ready_text: This timeless wisdom from Swami Sivananda on 'Discipline of Speech' emphasizes radical honesty ('Speak the truth at all cost'), conciseness ('Speak a little'), and profound kindness ('Speak sweetly', 'Always utter encouraging words'). It strongly advises against destructive communication, stating, 'Never condemn, criticize or discourage,' and promotes respectful interaction by cautioning, 'Do not raise your voice and shout at little children or subordinates.' This guidance is crucial for cultivating emotional intelligence, fostering empathy, and practicing self-control in all interactions, helping to prevent communication breakdowns, anger issues, and build stronger relationships and leadership. It's a call to mindful, compassionate, and disciplined communication that positively impacts mental health and spiritual growth.
